summary:
Astrolinc is a prototype that helps astronauts and ground support monitor health information during space missions. Astronauts can record and review vital signs, sleep, mood, and symptoms, while monitors can view crew information, send recommendations, and communicate with astronauts.

The system brings health information, alerts, reminders, and communication into one interface. It also includes an interactive 3D human model and features designed to help users explore symptom-related information. By making health information easier to access and share, AstroHealth aims to support awareness and communication when crews are far from Earth.

Astrolinc is a decision-support prototype, not a medical device. Its guidance and sample content require professional review and should not be treated as a diagnosis or an approved mission protocol.
details:
Astrolinc is a web-based prototype with two main roles: Astronaut and Monitor.

Astronauts can view their dashboard, record health information, review symptoms, receive reminders and recommendations, and communicate with ground support. The interface also includes an interactive 3D human model and an activity heatmap.

Monitors can review astronaut information, send recommendations and reminders, and communicate with astronauts. The project uses a React and TypeScript frontend, an ASP.NET Core backend, and SignalR for real-time communication. The frontend is hosted on Vercel, and the backend is hosted on MonsterASP.

The project’s goal is to make health information easier to review and share in a space-mission setting. Its guidance is non-diagnostic, and its medical content requires professional review before any real-world use.
